items.title: 68099_Erskine Hawkins oral history interview
items.q: He and I were still friends up until the time he passed.

ctx.x: What kind of places did you have to hear music because you mentioned that you were too young to actually go in to hear some of these players, but you wanted to hear them. What kind of places did you have, or opportunities did you have to hear live musicians?

Well, in Birmingham and at the school, at the school a lot of bands come through with Earl Hines during those years. And, Earl Hines came back to New York. He'd tell Joe Glaser all about that. And, that's the only place that I actually did hear was in Birmingham. That was at the Elks Place. That's where they said I was too young to get in. So. I used to stand outside and try to look through the windows cause I couldn't get in. And, all the other times, I couldn't, this was just like radio.
I didn't go nowhere. I didn't go out. (Inaudible). That's kind of close.
